findings.title: A failed device-limit check is cached, allowing the next request through
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before storing it. When storage returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, this return propagates the error and the first authentication is rejected, but the cache entry is not removed. The next request with the same device ID hits the cache and returns success without checking the limit, so a retry bypasses the configured cap. Remove the cache entry after a failed store or cache only successful stores.

findings.title: Concurrent registrations can exceed the configured device limit
findings.body: The limit check counts devices separately from the later insert, with no lock or atomic database constraint covering both operations. Concurrent requests for different device IDs can all observe a count below the limit and then insert, exceeding the configured maximum; this can also happen across Grafana instances sharing the database. Enforce the limit atomically across the count-and-insert operation.

findings.title: Document the new anonymous device-limit setting
findings.body: This reads `auth.anonymous.device_limit`, but the setting is not added to the shipped defaults or configuration reference. Administrators cannot discover the option or learn its default and semantics from Grafana's configuration documentation. Add a documented `device_limit` entry, including that zero disables the limit.
